before: Physical left and right stay on those sides. Logical inline-start and inline-end follow the text’s writing direction.
For horizontal left-to-right text, inline-start is left. For horizontal right-to-left text, inline-start is right.

Logical spacing can adapt without separate left and right rules.
```css
.note { padding-inline-start: 16px; padding-inline-end: 4px; }
```
The HTML dir attribute expresses text direction. CSS logical properties respond to that direction; they do not translate the content.
Block-start and block-end follow the other layout axis. Vertical writing modes change the mapping, so do not define logical properties as permanent synonyms for top or left.
The practice uses horizontal writing only. Check both directions instead of looking at one note and assuming the other adapts.
after: Some languages read from left to right. Others read from right to left. Logical spacing uses the start and end of the text direction instead of fixed left and right sides.
For horizontal text, `inline-start` is the left edge when reading left to right. It is the right edge when reading right to left.
The HTML `dir` attribute sets text direction. `ltr` means left to right. `rtl` means right to left. These spacing rules follow that setting; they do not translate the words.
`block-start` and `block-end` follow the direction lines stack. In this horizontal page, they mean top and bottom. Vertical writing can use different edges.
This practice uses horizontal text. Check both notes to see the larger space move to the correct start edge.

before.question: A horizontal note changes from dir=ltr to dir=rtl. What happens to padding-inline-start?
choices: It stays on the physical left
before.explanation: Inline-start follows the beginning of the inline writing direction. In horizontal RTL text that side is the right.

after.question: A horizontal note changes from left-to-right to right-to-left. Where does padding-inline-start go?
choices: It becomes space outside the box
after.explanation: Inline-start follows the start of the text. Right-to-left text starts on the right.
